name: Leutascher Geisterklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Leutasch Spirit Gorge: spectacular rocky gorge on the border with Bavaria with a 970 m steel walkway, daring panoramic bridge, and goblin trail.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Leutascher Geisterklamm (also known as Leutaschklamm or Leutasch Spirit Gorge) is a spectacular, deeply cut rocky gorge on the border between the Tyrolean high plateau of Leutasch/Seefeld and the Bavarian market town of Mittenwald. The untamed Leutascher Ache river rages through the narrow valley, having carved its way deep into the hard Wetterstein limestone over millennia. Since its opening in 2006, this cross-border gorge has been considered a masterpiece of Alpine trail construction, delighting families, geology enthusiasts, and hikers with a daring, seemingly free-floating walkway system directly above the roaring white water.

Route & Requirements

The development of the previously inaccessible natural gorge was carried out as part of an Austrian-German EU community project. The absolute highlight is the approximately 970-meter-long Klammgeistweg (Spirit Gorge Trail): a daring construction of galvanized gratings and sturdy railings anchored horizontally directly into the vertical, up to 100-meter-high rock faces. Hikers look through the gratings directly down into the gurgling whirlpools and emerald green pools of the Ache river. The climax of the route is the Panoramabrücke (Panoramic Bridge): at a dizzying height of around 50 meters, the suspension bridge spans the gorge, offering breathtaking views over the Wetterstein Mountains and the Karwendel peaks.

Visit & Arrival

The Klammgeistweg and the Panoramic Bridge are freely and cost-free accessible daily around the clock during the snow-free months from early May to late October/November (closed by authorities for safety reasons in case of ice, snow, or storms). Optional access to the small waterfall trail near Mittenwald costs approx. €4.00 for adults. Arrival by car: From Seefeld in Tyrol on the L14 through the Leutasch valley to the district of Schanz (large paid hiking car park directly at the beginning of the gorge trail). Alternatively, arrival via Mittenwald (P1/P2 Klamm). By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Seefeld in Tyrol train station, from there the regional VVT bus line 430 runs through the Leutasch valley directly to the Leutasch Schanz stop.

Tips

The steel grating walkway is largely flat and wide enough for pedestrians, but requires a head for heights; for standard strollers and wheelchairs, the walkway is only partially suitable due to individual steps and grating floors (dogs are allowed, but many four-legged friends avoid the gratings). Plan about 1.5 to 2 hours walking time for the circular route over the Panoramic Bridge. After the tour, the traditional inn Zur Schanze invites you to enjoy Tyrolean dumpling soups and refreshments, offering fascinating insights into the rich cultural history of the Tyrolean Alps.
preis: Klammgeistweg and panoramic bridge freely accessible at no cost
oeffnungszeiten: Early May to late Oct/Nov daily freely accessible (closed in winter)
